title: POC velocity checkpoint - flow calibration
meeting_header: Date: 2027-07-22 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Bridge: Zoom | Recording: enabled | Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Jordan (Redwood) + Lena, Marcus, Priya (Fluxion)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput numbers after three days of steady traffic shaping. Reviewed telemetry: token/sec, batching effectiveness, queue depth distribution. Tuned continuous batching threshold and lowered per-instance concurrency target to reduce tail latency spikes. Agreed to run 12-hour stability run with new batch settings and provide per-model breakdown. Action items assigned for benchmark spreadsheet and security doc follow-up.
questions: What is Fluxion's target 95th pct latency under 100 RPS?
Can Redwood run a 12-hour stability run with current model weights?
Do we require VPC/private deployment for pilot scale?
action_items: Maya Patel - Share updated benchmark spreadsheet with per-model tokens/sec and latencies - 2027-07-24
Ethan Wu - Apply continuous batching tweak (min_batch_timeout 6ms -> 4ms) and deploy to test slice - 2027-07-23
Marcus Bell - Provide representative traffic trace (1 week) and top-3 prompt families - 2027-07-25
Jordan Crane - Send SOC2 summary + redacted audit logs access instructions - 2027-07-26
next_steps: Run 12-hour stability test overnight (new batch settings) and capture 50/95/99 latencies and token/sec per model
Redwood to share micro-dashboard link with per-route latency percentiles
Fluxion to confirm decision criteria for dedicated vs hosted by next check-in
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena (Fluxion SRE): Lena here. Marcus and Priya are on.
[00:09] Marcus (Fluxion): Hey.
[00:12] Ethan (Redwood SE): Ethan here — I did the deployment tweak last night, so we'll walk through numbers.
[00:18] Maya: Cool. The agenda: throughput recap, continuous batching tweak results, queueing anomalies, then action items. Any other items?
[00:25] Priya (Fluxion): No, that's good. We're mainly interested in steady-state cost/perf tradeoffs.
[00:30] Ethan: OK I'll start. So we've got 72 hours of telemetry after the initial batch profile change. High level: average tokens/sec per instance up ~14%, token cost down roughly 7% in the hosted slice. But we saw 95th latency regressions on the long-tail prompts at peak.
[01:00] Lena: Can you clarify, is that at 200 RPS or when traffic bursts hit 350? Our traffic is pretty spiky at 4pm UTC.
[01:08] Ethan: Good question. The regressions correlated with transient bursts >300 RPS. At steady 100-150 RPS we meet the 95th target.
[01:20] Maya: Quick primer — continuous batching reduced per-token overhead but it increases queueing depth slightly which can increase tail latencies for long sequences. We tuned min_batch_timeout down to 6ms to favor sooner dispatch.
[01:35] Marcus: I remember the earlier recommendation to reduce concurrency per model; did that land?
[01:40] Ethan: We lowered per-instance concurrency from 16 to 12 for the large-ctx model. That reduced queuing at the model level but increased per-token compute because fewer concurrent contexts were active. Net effect was cost savings but tail got worse under burst.
[02:05] Priya: Do you have a suggestion for a sweet spot? Our SLO is 95th <= 450ms for health-critical flows.
[02:12] Ethan: For your workload I recommend targeting instance concurrency 10-12 and sharper queue shaping: prioritize short prompt families into fast lane and cap long-run requests with optional queuing policy. Also consider smaller quantized model variant as fallback.
[02:35] Lena: The priority lanes sound interesting — can Redwood do request classification at the router level?
[02:40] Maya: Yes, we can deploy a lightweight router rule set: route by prompt hint or header, or use prefix signature hashing. It's an opt-in config. We'll draft examples.
[02:55] Speaker 1: (murmur) 
[03:10] Ethan: I want to show the dashboard snapshot — tokens/sec, batch size distribution, queue depth histogram. (screen share noise)
[03:30] Ethan: So here, you can see batch size median is 8, but mean is 11 — that skew explains some variance. We targeted continuous batching threshold at 10 but bursts pushed many batches larger which helped throughput but hurt tail for long prompts.
[04:05] Marcus: Is there a way to bound batch size to protect latency?
[04:10] Ethan: Yes, you can set a max_batch_size and an adaptive timeout. For example max_batch_size 12 and min_batch_timeout 4ms gives good tradeoffs in our tests.
[04:25] Priya: Any impact on overall cost if we cap batch size?
[04:30] Ethan: Slightly—capping can drop efficiency by ~3-5%, but reduces 95th by up to 30% in taily cases. It's a cost/latency trade.
[05:00] Lena: On the queueing anomalies: we saw one spike where queue depth hit 480 at 16:12 UTC and a couple of p95 jumps. Root cause?
[05:12] Ethan: That aligned with an upstream client retry storm. It also found a little bug in our fallback policy where fallback model selection delayed for 200ms while checking variant availability. We fixed that in the test slice; will roll to pilot if stability run looks good.
[05:38] Maya: That bug fix should reduce the amplification on retry storms. Also will add stricter deadline enforcement at the router.
[05:48] Marcus: For the stability run — what metrics should we expect in the artifact?
[05:52] Ethan: We'll provide hourly aggregates: tokens/sec, mean/50/95/99 latencies, batch size percentiles, queue depth percentiles, concurrency per instance, fallback invocation rate.
[06:10] Priya: And will you include per-prompt family breakdown?
[06:14] Ethan: Yes capture top-10 prompt signatures. Marcus, if you can provide a representative trace we can map those signatures.
[06:23] Marcus: I'll export last week's traces and upload.
[06:26] Lena: Security question — we need to see audit log retention and KMS flow for the private slice.
[06:32] Jordan (CSM): I can share the SOC2 summary and a redacted log export process. You mentioned KMS — Redwood integrates with customer KMS via our Private deployment.
[06:45] Priya: For pilot scale we probably won't go private yet, but we want the path documented.
[06:50] Maya: Understood. We'll send the private deployment runbook and an example KMS integration pattern.
[07:00] Ethan: Back to tuning: I'm going to try two changes in the test slice after the call: min_batch_timeout 6ms -> 4ms, and max_batch_size 12. Also I'll reduce concurrency to 10 for the large model only.
[07:18] Maya: Sounds good. We'll kick off a 12-hour stability run tonight at 22:00 UTC; capture artifacts and notify you when complete.
[07:28] Marcus: If you could also annotate the dashboard with the exact deploy times that'd help correlate with client-side retries.
[07:33] Ethan: Yep will add deploy annotations.
[07:38] Lena: One last nit — do we have cost projection for projected steady-state at 200 RPS?
[07:44] Maya: We'll update the benchmark spreadsheet with a 200 RPS steady-state column and an estimated monthly spend. I'll include that in the spreadsheet I'm sharing.
[07:55] Priya: Great. Any blockers?
[07:58] Marcus: Nope from infra side.
[08:01] Maya: OK let's recap action items and next steps.
[08:06] Ethan: Recap — apply the batching changes to test, run 12-hour stability, collect per-prompt metrics, provide dashboard link and annotated deploys.
[08:14] Jordan: I'll send SOC2 excerpt and log redaction steps.
[08:18] Maya: Marcus to upload representative trace. Marcus: deadline 7/25.
[08:24] Marcus: Yep.
[08:26] Lena: We'll reconvene same time next week unless something urgent pops up.
[08:30] Maya: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.
notes: Ethan to attempt min_batch_timeout reduction and max_batch_size cap in test slice
Dashboard link to be shared with hourly aggregates and per-prompt family breakdown
